newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Typhoon Winnie kills 25 in Taiwan, 15 missing.
newsitem.headline: Typhoon Winnie kills 25 in Taiwan, 15 missing.

text.p: A typhoon killed 25 people in Taiwan on Monday and Tuesday and rescuers were searching for 15 people missing after a hillside security wall and 10 residential blocks collapsed.

Rescue teams worked through the night and had found two more bodies by Tuesday afternoon -- a son who died in the arms of his father -- bringing to 13 the number of people killed by the collapse, police said.
Forty-eight people were injured, police added.
Typhoon Winnie, which hit northern Taiwan on Monday, has resulted in at least 25 deaths from landslides and floods that turned streets into rivers, police said.
Rescue authorities said they had sent more than 400 fire, military and police workers to search for survivors in the collapsed blocks in the Taipei county of Hsichih.
But debris packing the first and second floors of the fallen buildings made the operation slow and difficult.
The five-storey apartment complex gave way after a landslide toppled a security wall that crashed into the structure, police said.
"The whole scene looks as if it has gone through an explosion," a witness said.
Torrential rain from Typhoon Winnie swamped houses in low-lying areas of Taipei. Many roads were flooded and scores of cars and other vehicles submerged.
The typhoon, packing maximum sustained winds of 144 km per hour (89 miles per hour) and gusts of up to 180 kph (112 mph), forced government offices, financial markets and schools to close on Monday.
Most had reopened on Tuesday, officials said.
The provincial government said Winnie inflicted T$202.34 million (US$7.22 million) worth of agricultural damage across the country, according to preliminary estimates.
